crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Resection Planning and Margins
children.blurb: Resection planning and margins covers the use of AI to define what tissue must be removed during cancer or other surgery and to confirm that the remaining tissue is free of disease.

children.name: Haptic Feedback in Robotic Surgery
children.blurb: Haptic feedback in robotic surgery covers the sensing, transmission, and display of force, vibration, and tissue compliance information between a surgical robot's instruments and the surgeon at a console.

children.name: Virtual Surgical Rehearsal
children.blurb: Virtual surgical rehearsal uses patient-specific imaging and computational models to let a surgical team practice a planned procedure before entering the operating room.

children.name: Tremor Stabilisation in Microsurgery
children.blurb: Tremor stabilisation in microsurgery covers technologies that reduce or cancel physiological hand tremor during delicate procedures such as retinal, vascular, and neurosurgery.

children.name: Remote Telesurgery
children.blurb: Remote telesurgery is the practice of performing surgical procedures on a patient from a distance using robotic instruments, telecommunication links, and real-time imaging.

sections.body: Surgical robotics and navigation is the use of AI to help plan, guide, and perform operations. In practice, AI now helps outline the area to remove in cancer surgery, filters out hand tremor during fine movements, and lets a surgeon rehearse a specific patient's anatomy before the real cut. Haptic feedback systems translate sensor data into forces the surgeon feels, so the robot can signal when it is pressing on tissue. Remote telesurgery uses AI to manage network delay and keep instruments stable over distance. These are working tools in operating rooms, not lab concepts.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The field is uneven. Resection planning and tremor stabilisation are the most mature, with cleared devices in regular use for orthopaedic and neurosurgical procedures. Haptic feedback is still limited because force sensing at the instrument tip is expensive and fragile. Virtual rehearsal works well for anatomy visualisation but does not yet predict how living tissue will deform during surgery. Remote telesurgery has been demonstrated over long distances, but it depends on network quality and is not routine. The site tracks 6 active product liability and wrongful death lawsuits against AI companies, which shows that even approved systems can fail in ways that matter. Honest limits include narrow training data, poor generalisation to unusual anatomy, and the fact that the surgeon still carries final responsibility.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader looking for how AI decides what tissue to remove should start with Resection Planning and Margins, which covers tumour boundary detection and safety margins. Haptic Feedback in Robotic Surgery explains the sensor and actuator loop that gives a surgeon a sense of touch through a machine. Virtual Surgical Rehearsal is the page for patient specific simulation before an operation, while Tremor Stabilisation in Microsurgery focuses on the filters and control loops that cancel hand shake in eye and nerve work. Remote Telesurgery ties these together over distance, showing how planning, feedback, rehearsal and stabilisation must work when the surgeon is not in the room. Together the five pages move from before the cut to during it, and from local to remote.
